feature: Inject JIRA ticket summary into hypothesis prompt to break D3 wrong-mechanism ceiling
evaluator_verdict: PASS (AC-1 through AC-4 + edge cases + temporal safety). AC-5 PASS with corrected commit-time keys (D3=0.35, D1=0.90).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: When jira_summary is present in InvestigationContext, hypothesis prompt contains ## Ticket Context block with title and issue type
AC-2: When jira_summary is absent, prompt is identical to today's baseline (no regression)
AC-3: --jira-csv flag loads commit→JIRA mapping; per-commit jira_context_status logged in forensics JSON (injected | unavailable)
AC-4: Unit tests for context injection and absent-jira fallback — 465+ tests pass
AC-5: Mini n=20 with --jira-csv: D3 ≥ 0.35 AND D1 not regressed below 0.72
edge_cases: JIRA key absent in CSV — graceful skip, no error, status='unavailable'
JIRA title contains fix-commit language — inject title only (no description/resolution)
CSV has multiple JIRA keys per commit — use first key
verification_method: pytest (AC-1 to AC-4), n=20 eval run (AC-5)
temporal_safety: Only title + issue_type injected. Description and resolution excluded — may contain fix-commit details. This is acknowledged as oracle-adjacent (ticket created post-commit) but controlled: title reveals defect category, not fix location.
